params.body:
Attio knew a person's company only from their mail domain. Anyone on gmail, telenet or a similar mailbox had none, and the company typed on the contact form went into a note only.

What changes:

- **New person field `gentells_company`** ("Gentells company", text). `gentells:attio-setup` creates it and leaves the existing fields alone.
- **Billing details** record a new outbox event `customer.details` (user, customer, email, legal name, country, VAT number) each time they are saved. Attio then:
  - sets Gentells company to the legal name;
  - names the company record after it when the address has a business domain;
  - adds the note "gentells.com: billing details" with the organisation, country and VAT number.

  The legal name is checked against VIES for EU buyers, so it is the most reliable company name Gentells gets.
- **Contact form:** the typed company now also fills Gentells company, besides the note.
- **Backfill:** customers who saved billing details before this event existed get one `customer.details` per user, once. Running it again adds nothing.

The signup form stays as it is. A free account needs no organisation, and a paying one gives it with the billing details.

After merge, on the site server: `php artisan gentells:attio-setup`, then `gentells:attio-backfill --dry`, then `gentells:attio-backfill`.

Tests: `AttioTest` gains five cases (billing details on a gmail address and on a business domain, the event recorded on save, the backfill once, company from the contact form). AttioTest, BillingFlowTest, BillingTest and ContactFormTest pass (64). In the full suite 661 pass; the 9 failures are local OAuth keys and the build stamp, the same as on main.
params.title: Attio: the organisation a person gives, from billing details and the contact form
